title: streaming: lifecycle controls (client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, server timeouts)
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: streaming clients currently have rough edges around early cancel, network disconnects, and resuming long-lived streams. This causes wasted server work, poor UX for partial results, and complications for our OpenAI compatibility layer where clients expect resume/cancel semantics. This PR implements a lifecycle control protocol for streaming endpoints: 1) client-initiated cancel control frame (soft and hard cancel), 2) explicit disconnect detection and server-side work cancellation after a configurable grace period, 3) reconnect/resume support via short-lived session tokens and idempotent resume offsets, and 4) server idle/processing timeouts with observability hooks. Changes are backwards compatible: existing clients continue to receive delta chunks; new control frames are ignored by older clients. The OpenAI compatibility adapter now maps resume/cancel to a set of well-documented event types and preserves chunk ordering. Implementation summary: - Add lifecycle control frame parsing and validation in streaming handler and compat adapter. - Introduce SessionManager for short-lived stream sessions and token-based resume. - Track per-request cancellable contexts and expose a CancelReason metric. - Server enforces two timeouts: idle_timeout (default 30s) and processing_timeout (default 5m) configurable via env/config and surfaced in the console. - Add client tests, integration tests, and e2e scenario that simulates flaky networks and reconnects. - Update SDKs (Python/TS) with helper methods for sending control frames and resuming streams. - Minor API contract bump in the compat layer: new event types "control.cancel", "control.resume", and "control.resume_ack". See linked linear tickets for rollout plan and telemetry gating.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please add a unit test that simulates a mid-stream cancel with in-flight batch processing to ensure we don't leak GPU work. Also document the semantics for soft vs hard cancel.
Priya Nambiar: Added test that uses a fake executor and asserts work is aborted within processing_timeout. Soft cancel sends backlog drained event; hard cancel terminates KV cache and clears state.
Marina Lopez: Can we make the default idle_timeout 30s instead of 60s? We see many short-lived mobile connections and 60s keeps resources occupied.
Priya Nambiar: Lowered idle_timeout to 30s and added an env var REDWOOD_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT to override. Updated docs and console defaults.
Isaac Zhang: LGTM after nits. Please split the large SessionManager file into manager + store in a follow-up if you plan more features.
Priya Nambiar: Will follow-up with ENG-2410 to split SessionManager. Addressed nits and pushed a small refactor.

release_notes: - Add streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel (soft/hard), disconnect handling, reconnect/resume via session tokens. - Server defaults: idle_timeout=30s, processing_timeout=5m (configurable). - OpenAI compatibility adapter: new event types control.cancel, control.resume, control.resume_ack. - SDK helpers for resume/cancel in Python and TypeScript.
notes: Rollout plan: feature-flag behind runtime flag 'streaming_lifecycle_v2' then gradual rollout to hosted API customers.
Telemetry: new metrics streaming.cancel_count, streaming.resume_count, streaming.resume_latency_ms, streaming.cancel_reason.
Compatibility: old clients ignore control frames; compat adapter translates control events for OpenAI-like clients.
Follow-ups: ENG-2410 refactor SessionManager; ENG-2460 add resumable binary streams for embeddings pipelines.
